hints: Look closely at the shape and position of the chromosomes in each labelled cell. Which cell has chromosomes lined up in the middle, which has them pulled apart to opposite ends, and which has a dark solid nucleus with no visible chromosomes?
Remember DNA amount stays doubled from prophase through metaphase and only halves after sister chromatids separate in anaphase. Ask yourself which of R and T are both before that separation point.
walkthrough:
**Identify each cell stage from the photo**

Start by reading the chromosomes like a story. S has a dark, solid nucleus with no separate chromosomes, so this is interphase.

R shows long, thin, tangled chromosomes just becoming visible, so this is early prophase. T shows chromosomes lined up on the equator, so this is metaphase. P shows two sets of chromosomes moving to opposite poles, so this is anaphase. Q shows two new clumps reforming with a pinching cytoplasm, so this is telophase and cytokinesis.

**Test statements 1 and 2**

Statement 1 says P is anaphase. That matches what you see, two groups pulling apart, so statement 1 is correct.

Statement 2 says spindle formation is occurring in Q. Spindles form in prophase to move chromosomes, but Q is at the very end when the spindle is breaking down and nuclei are reforming. So statement 2 is false.

**Test statements 3 and 4 about DNA and order**

Statement 3 compares R (prophase) and T (metaphase). Both are after S phase DNA replication but before sister chromatids separate in anaphase, so both cells still contain the doubled amount of DNA. Statement 3 is correct.

Statement 4 gives S to R to T to P to Q. That is interphase to prophase to metaphase to anaphase to telophase, which is the perfect mitosis sequence. Statement 4 is correct.

Together, 1, 3 and 4 are correct.

**Pick the matching option**

1, 3 and 4 together is option C. Well done for linking what you see to what you know about the cycle.

options.A: Includes statement 2 which is false because Q is telophase, not spindle formation, and misses statement 4 which is true.
options.B: Includes statement 2 which is false and misses statement 3 which is true, since R and T both have doubled DNA before anaphase.
options.C: Correctly includes 1, 3 and 4. P is anaphase, R and T have the same doubled DNA content, and S to R to T to P to Q is the correct mitotic order.
options.D: Includes statement 2 which is false because spindle formation happens in prophase, not in telophase cell Q.
